prompt.context: Your client is a multinational pharmaceutical and biologics company that specializes in innovative therapies across different disease types. The company is forecasting that biosimilars, a drug compound that is designed to have active properties similar to those of a drug that has already been licensed, will be released by a competitor within the next 12 months that will be marketed as replacements to your top grossing blockbuster drugs causing a significant loss of revenue. Your client has a long history of revenue growth, and has hired you to see how it can continue to grow.
prompt.question: How can our client continue to grow revenue given the expected loss from biosimilar competition?

clarifying_info.q: How large is the client and what is the expected revenue impact?
clarifying_info.a: $50B a year in revenue. Revenue loss is forecasted at 5%, which is $2.5B a year — that is the number we are looking for.

clarifying_info.q: What does the competitive landscape look like?
clarifying_info.a: Lots of smaller and newer biotech companies with promising drug pipelines. The industry is shifting from blockbuster drugs to more personalized and targeted drugs with higher impact but smaller patient populations.

clarifying_info.q: What products does the client currently have?
clarifying_info.a: Currently commercializes 40 drugs with a very strong pipeline. The company has products in all major disease types but is known for its oncology drugs and believes oncology will continue to be the future of the company. There is a promising late-stage pipeline.

clarifying_info.q: What geographies are they in and what manufacturing capacity do they have?
clarifying_info.a: Already in all major global markets. Large and robust manufacturing facilities regionally located in the United States.
They want the $2.5B in revenue ASAP, would like at least a 50% ROI on any acquired assets, and costs are not an issue and should not be explored.

exhibits.title: Pipeline Asset Data
exhibits.shows: A table listing two pipeline drug assets (Red Pill and Blue Pill) with columns for Patient Population, Estimated Market Penetration %, Cost Per Treatment, # of Times Per Year To Take Treatment, and Chance of Making it to Market

exhibits.title: Cost to Acquire Company and Revenue Generated ($M)
exhibits.shows: A bar chart comparing three acquisition targets — Oncology Company A, Oncology Company B, and Immunology Company A — showing their acquisition cost and projected revenue generated in millions of dollars

framework: Organic — Current Drug Pipeline: assess late-stage assets' timeline and revenue potential; evaluate whether any can launch within 12 months
Organic — Marketing Strategy: accelerate commercialization of existing drugs
Organic — Raise Pricing: evaluate pricing power on current portfolio
Inorganic — Acquire assets from a competitor
Inorganic — Joint venture with a competitor
Inorganic — Acquire a small biotech/pharma company

questions.prompt: Walk through the pipeline data in Exhibit 1 and calculate the expected revenue for each asset. What is the total expected revenue from the pipeline?
questions.guidance: Candidate should multiply patient population × market penetration × cost per treatment × treatments per year × probability of reaching market for each asset, then sum them. A strong candidate will note the total falls short of $2.5B and proactively flag the gap.

math.setup: Expected Revenue = Patient Population × Market Penetration % × Cost Per Treatment × # Treatments Per Year × Chance of Making it to Market
steps: Total pipeline expected revenue: $1,250M + $781.25M = $2,031.25M, just over $2B
math.answer: Red Pill: $1.25B; Blue Pill: ~$781M; Combined: ~$2.03B; Remaining gap: ~$500M

questions.prompt: How else can the client generate the remaining ~$500M in revenue? (Brainstorm, then evaluate Exhibit 2)
questions.guidance: Candidate should brainstorm inorganic avenues (acquisitions, JVs, licensing). Then using Exhibit 2, they should evaluate which acquisition target meets both the revenue target and the 50% ROI constraint, and recommend based on strategic fit.

math.setup: ROI = (Revenue - Cost) / Cost × 100%. Client needs revenue >= $500M from acquisition and ROI >= 50%.
steps: Oncology Company A: ROI = (600 - 400) / 400 = 200/400 = 50% ROI. Revenue contribution = $600M > $500M needed. Passes both criteria.
Oncology Company B: ROI = (650 - 500) / 500 = 150/500 = 30% ROI. Does NOT meet 50% ROI threshold.
Immunology Company A: ROI = (600 - 400) / 400 = 200/400 = 50% ROI. Passes both criteria numerically.
Oncology A vs Immunology A: same financial profile. Client is known for oncology expertise; oncology is the stated future of the company. Oncology A is the stronger fit.
math.answer: Recommend Oncology Company A: 50% ROI, $600M revenue, aligned with oncology expertise

brainstorming.prompt: How else can the client generate the additional ~$500M in revenue beyond the two pipeline assets?

categories.name: Acquisitions
ideas: Acquire a small biotech/pharma company with complementary pipeline
Buy rights to late-stage assets from another company
Acquire an oncology-focused company to reinforce core competency

categories.name: Partnerships & Joint Ventures
ideas: Joint venture with a competitor to co-develop or co-commercialize a drug
In-licensing deal for a promising compound nearing approval

categories.name: Commercial / Organic
ideas: Raise pricing on existing blockbuster drugs before biosimilar entry
Expand indications for existing drugs to grow addressable population

categories.name: Portfolio Optimization
ideas: Divest non-core assets and redeploy capital to high-growth areas
Focus marketing spend on highest-margin drugs

recommendation: Pursue both pipeline assets (Red Pill and Blue Pill) to generate ~$2B in expected revenue, addressing the majority of the $2.5B shortfall
Acquire Oncology Company A for $400M, generating $600M in revenue and achieving the required 50% ROI, closing the remaining ~$500M gap and aligning with the client's core oncology strategy
risks: Pipeline drugs may not reach market (Red Pill only 50% probability, Blue Pill only 25%), creating downside risk to revenue projections
Acquisition integration could be complex or slower than expected, delaying revenue realization
Biosimilar competition may erode more revenue than the 5% forecast if competitors gain rapid market share
next_steps: Conduct detailed due diligence on Oncology Company A before finalizing acquisition
Accelerate regulatory and commercialization timelines for Red Pill and Blue Pill
Develop contingency revenue plans in case pipeline assets are delayed or fail to reach market
